column7: 2026-11-04: parseBytes (branch storage-app): only plain numbers, 'B' and binary units KiB..YiB (case-sensitive). kB/MB/GB etc. deliberately NOT parsed yet - user must check with the storage team how they want them read; throw rather than guess.

2026-11-04: Storage team answer: their users paste sizes from Windows Explorer, so on this branch the units without 'i' are powers of 1024 (1 KB or 1 kB = 1024, 1 MB = 1048576). To be added in a later session; parseBytes currently still throws on them. First commit has only B + binary units.

2026-11-04: billing-svc: when SI units (kB, MB, GB…) are added to parseBytes here, they are strict powers of 1000 (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes), matching prettyBytes output. Reason: billing quotes in strict SI. This differs from storage-app (1024) - do not copy that rule. Until then they keep throwing.
